learning.learning_goal: Understand area as the amount of flat space inside a boundary, measured with equal square units.
learning.big_idea: Area measures coverage: equal squares cover a flat region without gaps or overlaps.
assumed_prior_knowledge: use rows and columns to organize a count
novice_success_criteria: explain why area uses equal square units
connect a rectangular array to multiplication

screens.label: Lesson 008 · Prototype
screens.title: How much flat space is inside?
screens.body: Imagine covering a tabletop with tiles. Area tells how much flat surface is inside the outer edge. Equal square tiles let us count that space.
screens.callout: No area formula is assumed. A row runs across; a column runs up and down. We will count square tiles in rows before writing a multiplication rule.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Flooring and trim do not measure the same thing.
screens.prompt: A 4-by-3 floor needs tile across its entire surface. What must be measured?

choices.text: Only the line around the outside
The flat region inside the boundary
choices.feedback: Flooring covers the interior region, so the measurement must account for all of the space inside.

choices.text: Only the four corner points

hints: Imagine what the tiles must cover.
The outside edge does not include the middle of the floor.

screens.label: Observe
screens.title: Cover the interior with equal squares.

visual.ariaLabel: A rectangle covered by three rows of four equal square units
visual.caption: 3 rows × 4 squares in each row
visual.message: Twelve equal squares cover the region without gaps or overlaps.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: Why does multiplication measure this area?

visual.ariaLabel: Three rows with four equal square units in every row
visual.message: Each row has 4 square units, and there are 3 equal rows.

choices.text: Because 4 + 4 + 4 and 3 × 4 both count the 12 covering squares
choices.feedback: Multiplication is an efficient count of the equal square units arranged in rows and columns.

choices.text: Because every rectangle has an area of 12
Because only the outside squares count

hints: Count one full row, then count how many rows there are.
Multiplication can describe equal groups of squares.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Name the region, unit, and measurement.

visual.ariaLabel: A rectangle covered by ten equal square units
visual.message: The inside is covered by 10 equal squares, so its area is 10 square units.

screens.phraseMeaning: The amount of two-dimensional space covered inside a boundary

definitions.meaning: the flat space whose coverage is being measured
a square with sides 1 unit long, used as one unit of coverage
the number of equal square units needed to cover a region

screens.guidance: Before calculating, ask: What flat space am I covering, and what square unit am I using?

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Cover inside; count equal squares.
screens.hook: Area = equal square units covering the inside.
screens.body: The multiplication rule comes from counting a rectangular array, not from memorizing unexplained words.
rebuildSteps: Identify the flat region inside the boundary.
Cover the region without gaps or overlaps.
Count rows × squares per row and label the answer in square units.
screens.boundary: This rows-times-columns rule directly measures rectangles. Other shapes may need to be split, rearranged, or measured with a different area rule.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which statement explains a 5-by-3 rectangle?

visual.ariaLabel: A rectangle covered by three rows of five equal square units
visual.message: Three rows each contain five square units.

choices.text: 5 + 3 = 8 units because only two sides matter
5 × 3 = 15 square units because the array has 3 rows of 5
choices.feedback: The product counts every equal square covering the rectangle.

choices.text: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 square units because the border is the inside

hints: Count the squares, not the side lengths by themselves.
Use rows × squares in each row.

screens.label: Reveal
screens.title: The formula is a compressed square count.

visual.ariaLabel: Fifteen equal squares arranged in three rows and five columns
visual.message: Length and width describe the two directions of the square array.

screens.equation: Area = length × width = 5 units × 3 units = 15 square units

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: Find the coverage of a 6-by-2 garden bed.

visual.ariaLabel: A garden bed represented by two rows of six equal square units
visual.message: The model contains 2 rows of 6 square units.

choices.text: 8 square units, because 6 + 2 = 8
16 units, because 6 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 16
12 square units, because 2 × 6 counts all covering squares
choices.feedback: The two equal rows contain six square units each, for 12 square units of coverage.

hints: Count how many squares are in one row.
Multiply that count by the number of rows.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Reason without the grid.
screens.prompt: A rectangular rug is 5 feet long and 4 feet wide. How much floor does it cover?

choices.text: 18 square feet, because 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18
20 square feet, because 5 rows of 4 square feet cover the rug
choices.feedback: The rug covers a rectangular array of 5 × 4 equal square feet.

choices.text: 9 feet, because 5 + 4 = 9

hints: The question asks how much floor is covered.
Imagine one-foot squares arranged across the rug.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Reconstruct area from its meaning.
screens.prompt: Why is area reported in square units?

choices.text: Because equal squares cover a two-dimensional region
choices.feedback: Square units measure coverage in two directions: across and down the region.

choices.text: Because every shape has four square corners
Because square units measure only the outside edge

hints: Think about the unit used to tile the inside.
A line measures one direction; a square covers space in two directions.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Recognize equal area in a new arrangement.
screens.prompt: One rectangle is 3 by 8. Another is 4 by 6. Why do they cover the same amount of space?

choices.text: Both products equal 24 square units
choices.feedback: Different dimensions can form arrays with the same total number of square units.

choices.text: Both rectangles have the same side lengths
Both boundaries must have the same distance around them

hints: Calculate the square-unit count for each rectangle.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: Which explanation shows understanding?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains area.

choices.text: Area is the distance traced around a shape.
Area counts equal square units covering the region inside a boundary.
Area is found by adding any two side lengths.

hints: Think about coverage rather than edging.
Name the unit that covers the inside.

screens.title: You rebuilt area from coverage.
screens.body: You connected the inside region, equal square units, arrays, multiplication, and square-unit labels.
screens.nextRecommendation: Continue to perimeter to distinguish coverage from boundary distance.
